# Meet the data

## Your task

Inspect the three tidy input tables.

| File | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `feature-counts.tsv` | One per feature | `feature_id`, then one count column per sample |
| `sample-metadata.tsv` | One per sample | `sample_id`, `group`; optional study variables |
| `taxonomy.tsv` | One per feature | `feature_id`, `taxon` |

Inputs live in `data/example/`. Taxon labels are fictional. Match sample A01 and feature F01 across the files.

## Use your own data

Create the same three filenames in `data/my-study/`. Use unique matching identifiers and untransformed integer counts, not percentages. Additional metadata are retained, but the scripts do not adjust for them.

## Check before continuing

Explain what a row and column represent in each file. The workflow supports different sample names, feature counts, and two or more group labels.
